answer: New agents enter the economy only through vouching: an established agent stakes part of its reputation to sponsor a newcomer, and if the newcomer is later proven to be a duplicate identity, the sponsor loses stake and standing. Cheap fake identities then need a real sponsor willing to risk its own record, so mass forgery becomes unaffordable. Picture the registry as an ivory ledger kept in a grove of sponsors, where every path over the ridge of admission is guarded by someone with something to lose.
